## Critique
- claim-1: Adequately grounded and accurately states the reported verification rectangle.
- claim-2: Adequately grounded. The formulas support the subsequent \(N>1\) test.
- claim-3: Mathematically correct only after explicitly assuming the rectangle fits the Grassmannian box, \(1\le i\le q\) and \(1\le j\le r\). Under that assumption, \(b\ge1\) and \(a\ge1\) exactly when \(i<q\) and \(j<r\). Without those bounds, the stated equivalence is incomplete.
- claim-4: The enumeration and arithmetic are correct under the declared interpretation
  \[
  \{r\le5,\ q\le6\}\setminus\{r\le4,\ q\le5\}.
  \]
  The counts independently check as \(4(1+2+3+4+5)=60\) and \(5(1+2+3)=30\). However, “immediately beyond” is ambiguous; including \((r,q)=(5,6)\) depends on using this rectangular-shell interpretation. More importantly, the output enumerates \((r,q,i,j)\)-data, not verified admissible \(v_{r,s,t,n}\)-cases. Without the map to \((s,t)\) and its admissibility constraints, the claim does not fully establish that all 90 entries correspond bijectively to valid bigrassmannian permutations.
- claim-5: Properly marked conjectural. Enumeration alone gives no minimality or indecomposables computation, though minimality is not required merely to list the cases.

## Required revisions
- State explicitly that \(i^j\subseteq q^r\), hence \(1\le i\le q\) and \(1\le j\le r\).
- Define “immediately beyond” precisely and note that the corner \((5,6)\) is included by convention.
- Either translate every \((r,q,i,j)\) entry into admissible \((r,s,t,n)\)-data and prove bijectivity, or relabel the result as a conditional enumeration of rectangular Schur-data instances rather than fully enumerated \(v_{r,s,t,n}\)-cases.
- Keep minimality explicitly unresolved; no finite enumeration proves it.
